comments.text: Just to provide another perspective, my husband and I starting using AirB&B just about two years ago and love it.  We have a lot of space, love cooking our own breakfast, coming and going as we please, and having total privacy.  What's so bad about taking out the garbage and treating other people's property like it's your own, and leaving it like you found it?  If you want to take a vacation where everything is in a place you expect it to be, and you are pampered and cleaned up after, great!  Air B&B is not for you.  For the AirB&B we use, we pay slightly more than an equivalent hotel room, and it is worth it.  Maybe it's because we just got involved recently.  I would not want to stay in a questionably clean room for $20.  Air B&B has apparently evolved now into something that is equivalent to a hotel room price but offers a completely different experience.  I think (and hope) it will survive this evolution and people like us will become the new customer base.  I would be sorry if it were not available anymore.

I have used Airbnb quite a bit and still use them. However, I do a lot of work on the front end.
I only stay in places that have a lot of positive reviews (in the 4.9 range or higher) and the host also has to be highly rated. I will usually reach out to the host to ask a question to check their communication and response time. I use Google Maps to look at the neighborhood and make sure there is some sort of free cancellation with the reservation. If it doesn’t have those things, I don’t book.
I really like Airbnb for international stays. Those a lot of times are cheaper than hotels and give you more space. Especially if you are staying for an extended period.
I like Airbnb but I also do the work and the research to make sure I know what I am getting.

Airbnbs are only smart in certain locations…in Austin its a total waste of money/time…In rural France, its amazing and makes sense…we payed $50 to stay in the middle of a middle-ages castle town…so its for certain places, not ever large US cities. London - yes. New Mexico - no. I think most of these ppl are talking domestic travel hence the high prices…I never overpaid at an Airbnb.
